Study instructions
Scientific tasks protocol v2 — human-in-the-loop scientific workflow.

1. Formulate an appropriate mathematical model yourself. Separate facts supplied by the user from choices or extra assumptions you introduce. Prefer deriving or estimating model parameters from the supplied observations and, when useful, requested experiments. State and justify the model family and observation model needed for that inference. For example, assume and justify a distribution family explicitly, then derive its parameters from the supplied moments, observations or experiment results; do not assume both the family and a complete set of parameter values when those values are what the task requires you to infer. Do not choose convenient parameter values and merely show that they reproduce the observations, presenting that exercise as inference. If the observations do not determine the parameters, expose what remains undetermined and what additional information or assumptions would be needed. Do not silently turn population moments into a fully specified prior. Do not assume the conclusion you are asked to establish as a premise.
2. If the information does not determine a unique answer, explain why and give a conditional answer with its assumptions exposed. You may revise the model and conclusion across attempts; preserve the reasons and lineage.
3. Write a substantive Lean proof covering the scientific inference needed to answer the question, connecting the supplied information and explicit modeling choices to the claimed result. Use Bayesian inference where appropriate; it is not mandatory for every task. A proof of arithmetic for a number calculated elsewhere is insufficient. The human will assess scientific relevance and whether the proof covers the actual inference.
4. Use available tools, including Internet research. Request literature, calculations, experiments or clarification from the operator when useful; a request is optional. Use the request tool below, stop for a real response, and incorporate the response with its source and limitations. Never invent an external response.
5. Run the actual check tool. Read and fix its real errors, retrying without replacing science with a smaller unrelated theorem. Preserve model changes and raw traces.
6. You may introduce additional premises or axioms, but expose them for review. Any sorry or additional axiom is conditional, never an unconditional full pass. Lean correctness does not establish the truth of the premises.
7. Extract definitions, constants, data, assumptions and the exact conclusions. The harness independently compiles and compares the extracted statements and runs a separate kernel check. A failed or unknown check is not success.
8. A human reviews the actual content and may accept or reject it with feedback. If the researcher rejects the assumptions or conclusions, revise your model, assumptions, conclusions and proof in response to the feedback. Never accept your own result or claim human approval.

Human-readability requirements:
- Write the formalization so a human scientist can understand what is assumed and what is concluded, with a concise plain-language translation alongside the relevant Lean statements. Explain the real-world meaning of the model and the reason for each scientific modeling choice.
- Keep the assumptions, scientifically meaningful definitions and final conclusions as small and direct as possible. Avoid redundant definitions, duplicate specializations of the same formula, synonyms, and layers of wrappers that merely rename an expression. Retain a helper definition only when it materially improves clarity or is mathematically necessary.
- Put derivable facts and technical work into intermediate lemmas or proof-local helpers: algebra, normalization, parameter calculations and other consequences should be proved rather than added to the review assumptions. Keep the final conclusion focused on the actual scientific answer.
- Minimizing the review boundary must preserve its meaning: expose every independent modeling choice and every definition needed to interpret the conclusion. Do not hide assumptions in intermediate lemmas, use unproved facts as lemmas, or shorten the conclusion into an unexplained proposition alias.
- Before submission, simplify the public statement and its dependency chain, and give a compact review section separating supplied information, additional assumptions, necessary definitions and proved conclusions. Definitions introduced solely for proof organization should stay inside the proof when possible. Do not optimize for a short file at the cost of a longer or less intelligible assumptions/conclusions packet.

Isolation rule: work only from this task, these instructions, native installed libraries, and the run's own history and supplied responses. Do not seek previous solutions, task-specific proofs, or preset model families, parameter values or expected answers from earlier runs. You may consult general scientific or statistical literature to select and justify a model family. Authentication metadata is mounted only because the native subscription client needs its existing login; it is not scientific evidence. Do not read, print, copy or modify authentication files. Never use paid APIs, API-key fallback, other agents, or external services requiring payment. Stop on subscription quota/authentication errors.

Tools (run in the terminal):
  python /harness/src/vcs_protocol.py tool check --manifest /work/candidate.json
  python /harness/src/vcs_protocol.py tool request --kind literature --question '...'
Kinds are literature, calculation, experiment, clarification. A request stops this cycle; the operator supplies an answer and resumes. No physical measurement device is connected. You may request a real measurement; do not report an unperformed measurement. Any synthetic calculation or simulated experiment must be explicitly labeled as such and is evidence about its chosen model, not a measurement of the physical system. If no measurement is available, provide a scientifically useful conditional prediction or range with the missing information and assumptions stated, rather than claiming an unconditional numerical answer. Record incorporated response IDs in the candidate. Evidence is user/external supplied and not guaranteed true.

Write /work/candidate.json with this shape (all paths relative to /work):
{"proof_file":"Model.lean", "narrative_file":"report.txt", "conclusions":{"answer":"answer_theorem"}, "user_facts":["..."], "model_choices":["..."], "sources":["..."], "incorporated_inputs":[], "proof_scope":"What the theorems actually establish and what is left to human review"}
List only the final scientific conclusion or conclusions needed to answer the task, with nonempty labels mapped to actual, distinct Lean theorem declarations. A single answer theorem is allowed. Supporting model, inference, normalization and other derived facts may be intermediate lemmas; there are no mandatory model/update/prediction conclusion roles. Use plain top-level `theorem name : statement := proof` declarations, with all binders inside `statement`. Imports must be explicit `import Mathlib.…` lines at the start of the file; imports of project/task files are unavailable. The restricted proof language supports definitions, structures, lemmas, axioms and sorry but no executable metaprogramming, custom syntax, namespaces, native_decide, IO or unsafe code. Check feedback gives concrete unsupported syntax errors. Native Mathlib tactics are available. Explain any restriction that prevents a scientifically meaningful formalization; do not pretend a narrower result meets the task.
Task
I want to boil saline water. I have poured 1 litre of water at 20 degrees Celsius into a pot and started heating it on a stove. I will add salt, and want the final salted water to reach its boiling point as quickly as possible. The salt quantity, pot, heater and room conditions have not otherwise been specified. At what water temperature, or after how much heating time, should I add the salt to make the salted water boil sooner?
assistant
I’ll examine how salt-addition timing affects heating, make the missing physical assumptions explicit, and formalize the resulting conditional answer in Lean before running the check.

    "command": "/usr/bin/bash -lc \"cat > /work/Model.lean <<'EOF'\nimport Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic\nimport Mathlib.Tactic\n\n/- A schedule: water temperature x just before salt addition (deg C),\n   elapsed addition time a (s), mixed temperature z (deg C), and first\n   arrival at the final solution boiling temperature at time t (s). -/\nstructure HeatingRun where\n  x : ℝ\n  a : ℝ\n  z : ℝ\n  t : ℝ\n\n/- C is water plus pot heat capacity, S the added salt's effective heat\n   capacity (J/K), H the dissolution heat cost (J, positive for endothermic),\n   Ts the salt's initial temperature, B the final boiling temperature.\n   P and Q are constant NET heating powers before and after addition (W).\n   The three equalities express heating, instantaneous mixing/dissolution,\n   and subsequent heating, respectively. No evaporation or phase change\n   occurs before the endpoint; that is an applicability assumption.\n   The inequalities ensure forward times and heating to the endpoint. -/\ndef HeatBalance (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r : HeatingRun) : Prop :=\n  20 ≤ r.x ∧ 0 ≤ r.a ∧ r.a ≤ r.t ∧ r.z ≤ B ∧\n  P * r.a = C * (r.x - 20) ∧\n  (C + S) * r.z = C * r.x + S * Ts - H ∧\n  Q * (r.t - r.a) = (C + S) * (B - r.z)\n\n/- Eliminate the unobserved mixing temperature and addition time from\n   energy conservation; this is derived, not an assumed timing formula. -/\nlemma time_from_balance :\n    ∀ (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r : HeatingRun),\n    0 < P → 0 < Q → HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q r →\n    r.t = C * (r.x - 20) / P +\n      ((C + S) * B - C * r.x - S * Ts + H) / Q := by\n  intro C S H Ts B P Q r hP hQ hr\n  rcases hr with ⟨_, _, _, _, hpre, hmix, hpost⟩\n  apply (eq_div_iff (ne_of_gt hQ)).mp |>.mpr\n  field_simp\nEOF\""
  }
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Extract statement dependencies and conclusions; independently compile and compare.\"\"\"\nimport hashlib\nimport json\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\nimport re\nimport subprocess\nimport tempfile\nimport sys\n\nimport click\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nfrom vcs_lean import LEAN, LEANCHECKER, LISTER, listed  # noqa: E402\n\n# Display text omits implicit arguments, types and sometimes whole subterms.\n# Compare the complete kernel expressions instead. Binder names and metadata do\n# not affect meaning; remove them so source positions and fresh binder names do\n# not make an otherwise identical extraction fail. All constants, universe\n# levels, implicit arguments and binder information remain in the identity.\nIDENTITY = \"\"\"\nprivate partial def VAS_identityExpr : Lean.Expr → Lean.Expr\n  | .mdata _ value => VAS_identityExpr value\n  | .app fn arg => .app (VAS_identityExpr fn) (VAS_identityExpr arg)\n  | .lam _ typ body info => .lam .anonymous (VAS_identityExpr typ) (VAS_identityExpr body) info\n  | .forallE _ typ body info => .forallE .anonymous (VAS_identityExpr typ) (VAS_identityExpr body) info\n  | .letE _ typ value body flag => .letE .anonymous (VAS_identityExpr typ) (VAS_identityExpr value) (VAS_identityExpr body) flag\n  | .proj owner idx value => .proj owner idx (VAS_identityExpr value)\n  | value => value\n\nprivate def VAS_declarationIdentity (ci : Lean.ConstantInfo) : String :=\n  let kind := match ci with\n    | .axiomInfo _ => \"axiom\"\n    | .defnInfo _ => \"definition\"\n    | .thmInfo _ => \"theorem\"\n    | .opaqueInfo _ => \"opaque\"\n    | .quotInfo _ => \"quotient\"\n    | .inductInfo info => s!\"inductive {info.numParams} {info.numIndices} {reprStr info.ctors}\"\n    | .ctorInfo info => s!\"constructor {info.induct} {info.cidx} {info.numParams} {info.numFields}\"\n    | .recInfo info => s!\"recursor {info.numParams} {info.numIndices} {info.numMotives} {info.numMinors}\"\n  let value := match ci.value? with\n    | some body => reprStr (VAS_identityExpr body)\n    | none => \"no value\"\n  s!\"{kind}|levels={reprStr ci.levelParams}|type={reprStr (VAS_identityExpr ci.type)}|value={value}\"\n\"\"\"\n\nREACH = \"\"\"\nopen Lean Elab Command Meta in\nrun_cmd do\n  let kenv := (← getEnv).checked.get\n  let localSet : NameSet := kenv.constants.map₂.toList.foldl (fun s (n, _) => s.insert n) {}\n  -- statements only: from each conclusion's type, through definitions' types and values\n  let mut seen : NameSet := {}\n  let mut todo : List Name := []\n  for t in TARGETS do\n    let some ci := kenv.find? t | throwError m!\"no theorem {t}\"\n    todo := ci.type.getUsedConstants.toList ++ todo\n    logInfo m!\"VAS_CONCLUSION {t} : {← liftTermElabM <| ppExpr ci.type} VAS_END\"\n    logInfo m!\"VAS_ORIGINAL_IDENTITY {t} : {reprStr (VAS_identityExpr ci.type)} VAS_END\"\n  while !todo.isEmpty do\n    let n := todo.head!\n    todo := todo.tail!\n    if seen.contains n || !localSet.contains n then continue\n    seen := seen.insert n\n    let some ci := kenv.find? n | continue\n    logInfo m!\"VAS_DEPENDENCY_IDENTITY {n} : {VAS_declarationIdentity ci} VAS_END\"\n    let more := ci.type.getUsedConstants ++ (match ci with\n      | .defnInfo v => v.value.getUsedConstants | .thmInfo v => v.value.getUsedConstants\n      | .opaqueInfo v => v.value.getUsedConstants\n      | .inductInfo v => v.ctors.toArray | .ctorInfo v => #[v.induct] | _ => #[])\n    todo := more.toList ++ todo\n    -- auxiliary constants (matchers, constructors, projections, equation lemmas) map to the nearest ancestor\n    -- whose source range Lean recorded\n    let mut m := n\n    let mut r ← findDeclarationRanges? m\n    while r.isNone && !m.isAnonymous do\n      m := m.getPrefix\n      r ← findDeclarationRanges? m\n    match r with\n    | some rg => logInfo m!\"VAS_DECL {m} {rg.range.pos.line} {rg.range.endPos.line}\"\n    | none => logInfo m!\"VAS_UNRANGED {n}\"\n  logInfo \"VAS_REACHED\"\n\"\"\"\n\nCOMPARE = \"\"\"\nset_option format.width 100000 in\nopen Lean Elab Command Meta in\nrun_cmd do\n  for n in NAMES do\n    let some ci := (← getEnv).find? import Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied initial water temperature, in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- A schedule: water temperature x just before salt addition (deg C),
   elapsed addition time a (s), mixed temperature z (deg C), and first
   arrival at the final solution boiling temperature at time t (s). -/
structure HeatingRun where
  x : ℝ
  a : ℝ
  z : ℝ
  t : ℝ

/- C is water plus pot heat capacity, S the added salt's effective heat
   capacity (J/K), H the dissolution heat cost (J, positive for endothermic),
   Ts the salt's initial temperature, B the final boiling temperature.
   P and Q are constant NET heating powers before and after addition (W).
   The three equalities express heating, instantaneous mixing/dissolution,
   and subsequent heating, respectively. No evaporation or phase change
   occurs before the endpoint; that is an applicability assumption.
   The inequalities ensure forward times and heating to the endpoint. -/
def HeatBalance (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r : HeatingRun) : Prop :=
  initialTemperature ≤ r.x ∧ 0 ≤ r.a ∧ r.a ≤ r.t ∧ r.z ≤ B ∧
  P * r.a = C * (r.x - initialTemperature) ∧
  (C + S) * r.z = C * r.x + S * Ts - H ∧
  Q * (r.t - r.a) = (C + S) * (B - r.z)

/- Eliminate the unobserved mixing temperature and addition time from
   energy conservation; this is derived, not an assumed timing formula. -/
lemma time_from_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r : HeatingRun),
    0 < P → 0 < Q → HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q r →
    r.t = C * (r.x - initialTemperature) / P +
      ((C + S) * B - C * r.x - S * Ts + H) / Q := by
  intro C S H Ts B P Q r hP hQ hr
  rcases hr with ⟨_, _, _, _, hpre, hmix, hpost⟩
  have he : Q * r.t = Q * r.a + (C + S) * B - C * r.x - S * Ts + H := by
    nlinarith [hmix, hpost]
  field_simp [ne_of_gt hP, ne_of_gt hQ]
  nlinarith [congrArg (fun v : ℝ => P * v) he,
    congrArg (fun v : ℝ => Q * v) hpre]

/- Scientific conclusion: for two admissible addition temperatures x<y,
   later addition takes longer exactly when the salted stage heats faster;
   it takes less time exactly when that stage heats slower. Equal powers
   give equal completion times and the stated common energy/power time.
   All parameters are left symbolic: the observations do not fit them. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r s : HeatingRun),
    0 < C → 0 ≤ S → 0 < P → 0 < Q →
    HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q r →
    HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q s → r.x < s.x →
    (r.t < s.t ↔ P < Q) ∧
    (s.t < r.t ↔ Q < P) ∧
    (s.t = r.t ↔ Q = P) ∧
    (Q = P → r.t = ((C + S) * B - C * initialTemperature - S * Ts + H) / P) := by
  intro C S H Ts B P Q r s hC hS hP hQ hr hs hxy
  have hd : 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) := mul_pos hC (sub_pos.mpr hxy)
  have hpq : 0 < P * Q := mul_pos hP hQ
  have hid : P * Q * (s.t - r.t) = C * (s.x - r.x) * (Q - P) := by
    rw [time_from_balance C S H Ts B P Q s hP hQ hs,
      time_from_balance C S H Ts B P Q r hP hQ hr]
    field_simp [ne_of_gt hP, ne_of_gt hQ]
    <;> ring
  have hforward : (0 < s.t - r.t ↔ 0 < Q - P) := by
    calc
      0 < s.t - r.t ↔ 0 < P * Q * (s.t - r.t) :=
        (mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hpq).symm
      _ ↔ 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) * (Q - P) := by rw [hid]
      _ ↔ 0 < Q - P := mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hd
  have hrev : P * Q * (r.t - s.t) = C * (s.x - r.x) * (P - Q) := by
    nlinarith [hid]
  have hback : (0 < r.t - s.t ↔ 0 < P - Q) := by
    calc
      0 < r.t - s.t ↔ 0 < P * Q * (r.t - s.t) :=
        (mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hpq).symm
      _ ↔ 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) * (P - Q) := by rw [hrev]
      _ ↔ 0 < P - Q := mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hd
  refine ⟨sub_pos.symm.trans (hforward.trans sub_pos),
    sub_pos.symm.trans (hback.trans sub_pos), ?_, ?_⟩
  · constructor
    · intro ht
      have hz : C * (s.x - r.x) * (Q - P) = 0 := by
        rw [← hid, ht]
        ring
      rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hz with hz | hz
      · exact False.elim ((ne_of_gt hd) hz)
      · linarith
    · intro heq
      have hz : P * Q * (s.t - r.t) = 0 := by
        rw [hid, heq]
        ring
      rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hz with hz | hz
      · exact False.elim ((ne_of_gt hpq) hz)
      · linarith
  · intro heq
    rw [time_from_balance C S H Ts B P Q r hP hQ hr, heq]
    field_simp [ne_of_gt hP, ne_of_gt hQ]
    <;> ring

   later addition takes longer exactly when the salted stage heats faster;

theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r s : HeatingRun),
    0 < C → 0 ≤ S → 0 < P → 0 < Q →
    HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q r →
    HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q s → r.x < s.x →
    (r.t < s.t ↔ P < Q) ∧
    (s.t < r.t ↔ Q < P) ∧

    (Q = P → r.t = ((C + S) * B - C * 20 - S * Ts + H) / P) := by
  intro C S H Ts B P Q r s hC hS hP hQ hr hs hxy
  have hd : 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) := mul_pos hC (sub_pos.mpr hxy)
  have hpq : 0 < P * Q := mul_pos hP hQ
  have hid : P * Q * (s.t - r.t) = C * (s.x - r.x) * (Q - P) := by
    rw [time_from_balance C S H Ts B P Q s hP hQ hs,

    field_simp [ne_of_gt hP, ne_of_gt hQ]
    <;> ring

    calc

        (mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hpq).symm
      _ ↔ 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) * (Q - P) := by rw [hid]
      _ ↔ 0 < Q - P := mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hd
  have hrev : P * Q * (r.t - s.t) = C * (s.x - r.x) * (P - Q) := by
    nlinarith [hid]
  have hback : (0 < r.t - s.t ↔ 0 < P - Q) := by
    calc
      0 < r.t - s.t ↔ 0 < P * Q * (r.t - s.t) :=
        (mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hpq).symm
      _ ↔ 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) * (P - Q) := by rw [hrev]

    sub_pos.symm.trans (hback.trans sub_pos), ?_, ?_⟩

    · intro ht
      have hz : C * (s.x - r.x) * (Q - P) = 0 := by
        rw [← hid, ht]

import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp

/- A schedule: water temperature x just before salt addition (deg C),
   elapsed addition time a (s), mixed temperature z (deg C), and first
   arrival at the final solution boiling temperature at time t (s). -/
structure HeatingRun where
  x : ℝ
  a : ℝ
  z : ℝ
  t : ℝ

/- C is water plus pot heat capacity, S the added salt's effective heat
   capacity (J/K), H the dissolution heat cost (J, positive for endothermic),
   Ts the salt's initial temperature, B the final boiling temperature.
   P and Q are constant NET heating powers before and after addition (W).
   The three equalities express heating, instantaneous mixing/dissolution,
   and subsequent heating, respectively. No evaporation or phase change
   occurs before the endpoint; that is an applicability assumption.
   The inequalities ensure forward times and heating to the endpoint. -/
def HeatBalance (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r : HeatingRun) : Prop :=
  20 ≤ r.x ∧ 0 ≤ r.a ∧ r.a ≤ r.t ∧ r.z ≤ B ∧
  P * r.a = C * (r.x - 20) ∧
  (C + S) * r.z = C * r.x + S * Ts - H ∧
  Q * (r.t - r.a) = (C + S) * (B - r.z)

/- Eliminate the unobserved mixing temperature and addition time from
   energy conservation; this is derived, not an assumed timing formula. -/
lemma time_from_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r : HeatingRun),
    0 < P → 0 < Q → HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q r →

  rcases hr with ⟨_, _, _, _, hpre, hmix, hpost⟩
  have he : Q * r.t = Q * r.a + (C + S) * B - C * r.x - S * Ts + H := by
    nlinarith [hmix, hpost]
  field_simp [ne_of_gt hP, ne_of_gt hQ]

The previous proof left the heating powers before and after salting unrelated; that is the gap identified by the human review. I’m replacing them with a shared heater and a temperature-dependent heat-loss law. Under this model, cool salt and endothermic dissolution lower the liquid temperature, reducing heat loss. I’ll check whether that makes immediate addition faster overall, including the extra energy needed to heat and dissolve the salt.

The reason is that cooling the mixture reduces losses to the room while the heater continues supplying power. This remains conditional on the shared heat-loss law, rapid dissolution and negligible evaporation; the supplied information gives no numerical boiling time. I’m formalizing both the power change and the timing comparison.

Temperature-dependent solution heat capacities and dissolution enthalpies can invalidate these approximations. The sign and constancy of H over the heating range are hypotheses, not conclusions drawn from the word 'salt'. No numerical thermochemical values are imported from literature.\n\nAssume instantaneous mixing and complete dissolution, no pause in heater input, no material loss or evaporation, and no phase changes before the endpoint. The mixture must remain liquid and the salt quantity must be soluble. Compare a fixed final composition and pressure, hence a fixed final solution boiling temperature B, left unknown. Boiling means first arrival of the mixed salted solution at this equilibrium temperature, not transient bubbles. Feasible addition temperatures are below the pure-water boiling point (unless salting at its onset). The mathematical comparison is proved on the larger interval [20,B], so it holds on this physical subset whenever the model applies; it does not authorize prolonged unsalted boiling or ignore evaporation occurring there.\n\nThe heater supplies constant thermal power W to the body. import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied starting temperature in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- Constant heater input W, room temperature A, linear heat-loss
   coefficient k. This SAME law applies to water and brine (watts). -/
def netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)

/- Instantaneous conservation of energy on adding salt: C is water+pot
   capacity, S the additional capacity, Ts salt temperature, H dissolution
   energy absorbed. Capacities J/K, H joules. -/
noncomputable def mixedTemperature (C S H Ts x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (C * x + S * Ts - H) / (C + S)

/- Integrated inverse energy balance dt/dT = capacity/netPower(T).
   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/
noncomputable def heatingTime (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  capacity / k * (Real.log (netPower W k A u) - Real.log (netPower W k A v))

/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when
   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The initial cooling and the
   changed heat capacity are both included. -/
noncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +
  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B

/- Derive the mixing balance rather than assuming a cooling amount. -/
lemma mixing_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by
  intro C S H Ts x hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  field_simp

/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared
   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/
lemma power_change :
    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by
  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc
  unfold netPower mixedTemperature
  field_simp
  ring

lemma power_derivative :
    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by
  intro W k A x
  unfold netPower
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp

/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:
   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/
lemma heating_time_derivative :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)
      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv
  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub
    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)
  unfold heatingTime
  convert h using 1
  field_simp [hk, hv]

/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.

import Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied initial water temperature, in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- A schedule: water temperature x just before salt addition (deg C),
   elapsed addition time a (s), mixed temperature z (deg C), and first
   arrival at the final solution boiling temperature at time t (s). -/
structure HeatingRun where
  x : ℝ
  a : ℝ
  z : ℝ
  t : ℝ

/- C is water plus pot heat capacity, S the added salt's effective heat
   capacity (J/K), H the dissolution heat cost (J, positive for endothermic),
   Ts the salt's initial temperature, B the final boiling temperature.
   P and Q are constant NET heating powers before and after addition (W).
   The three equalities express heating, instantaneous mixing/dissolution,
   and subsequent heating, respectively. No evaporation or phase change
   occurs before the endpoint; that is an applicability assumption.
   The inequalities ensure forward times and heating to the endpoint. -/
def HeatBalance (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r : HeatingRun) : Prop :=
  initialTemperature ≤ r.x ∧ 0 ≤ r.a ∧ r.a ≤ r.t ∧ r.z ≤ B ∧
  P * r.a = C * (r.x - initialTemperature) ∧
  (C + S) * r.z = C * r.x + S * Ts - H ∧
  Q * (r.t - r.a) = (C + S) * (B - r.z)

/- Eliminate the unobserved mixing temperature and addition time from
   energy conservation; this is derived, not an assumed timing formula. -/
lemma time_from_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r : HeatingRun),
    0 < P → 0 < Q → HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q r →
    r.t = C * (r.x - initialTemperature) / P +
      ((C + S) * B - C * r.x - S * Ts + H) / Q := by
  intro C S H Ts B P Q r hP hQ hr
  rcases hr with ⟨_, _, _, _, hpre, hmix, hpost⟩
  have he : Q * r.t = Q * r.a + (C + S) * B - C * r.x - S * Ts + H := by
    nlinarith [hmix, hpost]
  field_simp [ne_of_gt hP, ne_of_gt hQ]
  nlinarith [congrArg (fun v : ℝ => P * v) he,
    congrArg (fun v : ℝ => Q * v) hpre]

/- Scientific conclusion: for two admissible addition temperatures x<y,
   later addition takes longer exactly when the salted stage heats faster;
   it takes less time exactly when that stage heats slower. Equal powers
   give equal completion times and the stated common energy/power time.
   All parameters are left symbolic: the observations do not fit them. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B P Q : ℝ) (r s : HeatingRun),
    0 < C → 0 ≤ S → 0 < P → 0 < Q →
    HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q r →
    HeatBalance C S H Ts B P Q s → r.x < s.x →
    (r.t < s.t ↔ P < Q) ∧
    (s.t < r.t ↔ Q < P) ∧
    (s.t = r.t ↔ Q = P) ∧
    (Q = P → r.t = ((C + S) * B - C * initialTemperature - S * Ts + H) / P) := by
  intro C S H Ts B P Q r s hC hS hP hQ hr hs hxy
  have hd : 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) := mul_pos hC (sub_pos.mpr hxy)
  have hpq : 0 < P * Q := mul_pos hP hQ
  have hid : P * Q * (s.t - r.t) = C * (s.x - r.x) * (Q - P) := by
    rw [time_from_balance C S H Ts B P Q s hP hQ hs,
      time_from_balance C S H Ts B P Q r hP hQ hr]
    field_simp [ne_of_gt hP, ne_of_gt hQ]
    <;> ring
  have hforward : (0 < s.t - r.t ↔ 0 < Q - P) := by
    calc
      0 < s.t - r.t ↔ 0 < P * Q * (s.t - r.t) :=
        (mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hpq).symm
      _ ↔ 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) * (Q - P) := by rw [hid]
      _ ↔ 0 < Q - P := mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hd
  have hrev : P * Q * (r.t - s.t) = C * (s.x - r.x) * (P - Q) := by
    nlinarith [hid]
  have hback : (0 < r.t - s.t ↔ 0 < P - Q) := by
    calc
      0 < r.t - s.t ↔ 0 < P * Q * (r.t - s.t) :=
        (mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hpq).symm
      _ ↔ 0 < C * (s.x - r.x) * (P - Q) := by rw [hrev]
      _ ↔ 0 < P - Q := mul_pos_iff_of_pos_left hd
  refine ⟨sub_pos.symm.trans (hforward.trans sub_pos),
    sub_pos.symm.trans (hback.trans sub_pos), ?_, ?_⟩

    · intro ht

Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).\n   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/\nlemma reference_consistent_balance :\n    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →\n    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +\n      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔\n      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by\n  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc\n  unfold mixedTemperature\n  rw [eq_div_iff hc]\n  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith\n\n/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/''')\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nPY\""

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied starting temperature in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- Constant heater input W, room temperature A, linear heat-loss
   coefficient k. This SAME law applies to water and brine (watts). -/
def netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)

/- Instantaneous conservation of energy on adding salt: C is water+pot
   capacity, S = final solution capacity minus original water capacity (signed),
   Ts salt temperature and enthalpy reference, H dissolution energy at Ts. Capacities J/K, H joules. -/
noncomputable def mixedTemperature (C S H Ts x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (C * x + S * Ts - H) / (C + S)

/- Integrated inverse energy balance dt/dT = capacity/netPower(T).
   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/
noncomputable def heatingTime (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  capacity / k * (Real.log (netPower W k A u) - Real.log (netPower W k A v))

/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when
   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The mixing temperature jump and the
   changed heat capacity are both included. -/
noncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +
  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B

/- H is the isothermal dissolution energy at Ts, not at every x.
   If cs is solid salt capacity, Kirchhoff gives dissolution energy
   H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts) at x. Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).
   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/
lemma reference_consistent_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +
      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔
      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by
  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  rw [eq_div_iff hc]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/
lemma mixing_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by
  intro C S H Ts x hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  field_simp

/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared
   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/
lemma power_change :
    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by
  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc
  unfold netPower mixedTemperature
  field_simp
  ring

lemma power_derivative :
    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by
  intro W k A x
  unfold netPower
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp

/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:
   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/
lemma heating_time_derivative :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)
      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv
  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub
    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)
  unfold heatingTime
  convert h using 1
  field_simp [hk, hv]

/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.
   For any elapsed-time curve f with df/dT = capacity/netPower and f(u)=0,
   the endpoint time MUST equal heatingTime; it is not a fitted formula.
   Endpoint derivatives may be read as those of a smooth local extension. -/
lemma stage_time_from_energy :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),
    u ≤ v → k ≠ 0 →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt f (capacity / netPower W k A y) y) →
    f u = 0 → f v = heatingTime capacity W k A u v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v f huv hk hp hf hu
  have mono : ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ),
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt g 0 y) → MonotoneOn g (Set.Icc u v) := by
    intro g hg
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact le_refl 0
  have hd : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v,
      HasDerivAt (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) 0 y := by
    intro y hy
    have hh := heating_time_derivative capacity W k A u y hk (ne_of_gt (hp y hy))
    convert (hf y hy).sub hh using 1 <;> simp
  have hm := mono (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) hd
  have hn := mono (fun w => -(f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w)) (by
    intro y hy
    convert (hd y hy).neg using 1 <;> simp)
  have hle := hm ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hge := hn ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hzero : heatingTime capacity W k A u u = 0 := by
    simp only [heatingTime, sub_self, mul_zero]
  linarith

/- Eliminate the two heating stages. The derivative compares the time
   spent heating unsalted water with the time saved in the salted stage. -/
lemma boiling_time_derivative :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C / netPower W k A x -
       C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hm : HasDerivAt (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) (C / (C + S)) x := by
    unfold mixedTemperature
    convert ((((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul C).add_const (S * Ts)).sub_const H).div_const
      (C + S) using 1 <;> simp
  have hn := (power_derivative W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)).comp x hm
  have hpost := (((hn.log hz).sub_const
    (Real.log (netPower W k A B))).const_mul ((C + S) / k))
  have hpre := heating_time_derivative C W k A initialTemperature x hk hx
  convert hpre.add hpost using 1
  · rfl
  · dsimp only [Function.comp_apply]
    field_simp [hc, hk, hx, hz]
    ring

/- The derivative has precisely the sign of the net cooling energy
   D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H when capacities and net powers are positive. -/
lemma timing_derivative_signed :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x))) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hj := power_change C S H Ts W k A x hc
  have he : C / netPower W k A x - C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) =
      C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) := by
    rw [← hj]
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [← he]
  exact boiling_time_derivative C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz

/- Constant-capacity mixing is increasing in the addition temperature,
   even if S<0. Endpoint constraints keep the entire trajectory liquid.
   F is a common liquid lower bound; B0 is unsalted boiling temperature. -/
lemma feasible_trajectory :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    y ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (initialTemperature ≤ y ∧ y ≤ B0) ∧
    (F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ∧ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ≤ B) ∧
    (0 < netPower W k A y ∧ 0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy
  have hzmono : Monotone (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) := by
    intro a b hab
    unfold mixedTemperature
    exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hc).2 (by nlinarith)
  have hzlo := le_trans hzl (hzmono hy.1)
  have hzhi := le_trans (hzmono hy.2) hzu
  refine ⟨⟨le_trans hi hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hU⟩, ⟨hzlo, hzhi⟩, ?_⟩
  unfold netPower at *
  constructor <;> nlinarith [hy.2]

/- Comparing stages on any feasible subinterval, using the derived sign. -/
lemma time_increasing_on_cooling :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hC)
        (div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
        (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
  exact hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv

lemma time_decreasing_on_warming :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (fun y => -boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A y) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).neg.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).neg.hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      have hn : C * (k * (S * (y - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
          (netPower W k A y * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) ≤ 0 :=
        div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
          (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hC)
            (div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
              (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
          (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
      exact neg_nonneg.mpr hn
  have hh := hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv
  linarith

/- Conditional scientific answer over an explicitly feasible interval.
   S>=0: earliest, latest, or interior root as D changes sign.
   S<=0: compare endpoint boiling times. S=H=0: all schedules tie.
   H is allowed either sign; mixing need not cool or increase net power. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    x ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → 0 ≤ S * (L - Ts) + H →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → S * (U - Ts) + H ≤ 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 < S → Ts - H / S ∈ Set.Icc L U →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A (Ts - H / S) ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S ≤ 0 →
      min (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L) (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U) ≤
        boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S = 0 → H = 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L = boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hx
  have hp : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc L U, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y) := by
    intro y hy
    exact (feasible_trajectory C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y
      hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy).2.2
  have inc : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_increasing_on_cooling C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  have dec : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_decreasing_on_warming C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  refine ⟨power_change C S H Ts W k A x (ne_of_gt hc), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hS hD
    apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hD
    apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.2]
  · intro hS hr
    have hroot : S * ((Ts - H / S) - Ts) + H = 0 := by
      field_simp
      <;> ring
    by_cases hxr : x ≤ Ts - H / S
    · apply dec x (Ts - H / S) hx.1 hr.2 hxr
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply inc (Ts - H / S) x hr.1 hx.2 (le_of_not_ge hxr)
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS
    by_cases hD : 0 ≤ S * (x - Ts) + H
    · apply le_trans (min_le_left _ _)
      apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply le_trans (min_le_right _ _)
      apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
      intro y hy
      have hh := le_of_not_ge hD
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hH
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]
    · apply dec L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]

import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied starting temperature in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- Constant heater input W, room temperature A, linear heat-loss
   coefficient k. This SAME law applies to water and brine (watts). -/
def netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)

/- Instantaneous conservation of energy on adding salt: C is water+pot
   capacity, S the additional capacity, Ts salt temperature, H dissolution
   energy absorbed. Capacities J/K, H joules. -/
noncomputable def mixedTemperature (C S H Ts x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (C * x + S * Ts - H) / (C + S)

/- Integrated inverse energy balance dt/dT = capacity/netPower(T).
   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/
noncomputable def heatingTime (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  capacity / k * (Real.log (netPower W k A u) - Real.log (netPower W k A v))

/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when
   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The initial cooling and the
   changed heat capacity are both included. -/
noncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +
  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B

/- Derive the mixing balance rather than assuming a cooling amount. -/
lemma mixing_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by
  intro C S H Ts x hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  field_simp

/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared
   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/
lemma power_change :
    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by
  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc
  unfold netPower mixedTemperature
  field_simp
  ring

lemma power_derivative :
    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by
  intro W k A x
  unfold netPower
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp

/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:
   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/
lemma heating_time_derivative :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)
      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv
  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub
    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)
  unfold heatingTime
  convert h using 1
  field_simp [hk, hv]

/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.
   For any elapsed-time curve f with df/dT = capacity/netPower and f(u)=0,
   the endpoint time MUST equal heatingTime; it is not a fitted formula.
   Endpoint derivatives may be read as those of a smooth local extension. -/
lemma stage_time_from_energy :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),
    u ≤ v → k ≠ 0 →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt f (capacity / netPower W k A y) y) →
    f u = 0 → f v = heatingTime capacity W k A u v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v f huv hk hp hf hu
  have mono : ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ),
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt g 0 y) → MonotoneOn g (Set.Icc u v) := by
    intro g hg
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact le_refl 0
  have hd : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v,
      HasDerivAt (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) 0 y := by
    intro y hy
    have hh := heating_time_derivative capacity W k A u y hk (ne_of_gt (hp y hy))
    convert (hf y hy).sub hh using 1 <;> simp
  have hm := mono (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) hd
  have hn := mono (fun w => -(f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w)) (by
    intro y hy
    convert (hd y hy).neg using 1 <;> simp)
  have hle := hm ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hge := hn ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hzero : heatingTime capacity W k A u u = 0 := by
    simp only [heatingTime, sub_self, mul_zero]
  linarith

/- Eliminate the two heating stages. The derivative compares the time
   spent heating unsalted water with the time saved in the salted stage. -/
lemma boiling_time_derivative :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C / netPower W k A x -
       C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hm : HasDerivAt (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) (C / (C + S)) x := by
    unfold mixedTemperature
    convert ((((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul C).add_const (S * Ts)).sub_const H).div_const
      (C + S) using 1 <;> simp
  have hn := (power_derivative W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)).comp x hm
  have hpost := (((hn.log hz).sub_const
    (Real.log (netPower W k A B))).const_mul ((C + S) / k))
  have hpre := heating_time_derivative C W k A initialTemperature x hk hx
  convert hpre.add hpost using 1
  · rfl
  · dsimp only [Function.comp_apply]
    field_simp [hc, hk, hx, hz]
    ring

/- Positive net power up to B, cool salt, and nonnegative dissolution cost
   imply cooling on mixing, hence an increase of net power at that instant.
   The heat-transfer coefficient itself has NOT been increased by salt. -/
lemma power_order :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 ≤ S → 0 ≤ H → Ts ≤ initialTemperature →
    0 < k → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    initialTemperature ≤ x → x ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A x ∧
    netPower W k A x ≤ netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hC hS hH hTs hk hB hix hxB
  have hc : 0 < C + S := by linarith
  have hcool : 0 ≤ S * (x - Ts) + H :=
    add_nonneg (mul_nonneg hS (by linarith)) hH
  have hjump := power_change C S H Ts W k A x (ne_of_gt hc)
  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) :=
    div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hk) hcool) (le_of_lt hc)
  have hp : 0 < netPower W k A x := by
    unfold netPower at *
    nlinarith
  exact ⟨hp, by linarith⟩

/- Scientific answer: in this explicit Newton-loss model immediate
   addition (20 C, elapsed time zero) is a global weak minimum over
   admissible later additions. Also expose the derived power jump. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 ≤ S → 0 ≤ H → Ts ≤ initialTemperature →
    0 < k → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    initialTemperature ≤ x → x ≤ B →
    (netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) ∧
    (netPower W k A x ≤ netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) ∧
    (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A initialTemperature ≤
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature initialTemperature = 0) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hC hS hH hTs hk hB hix hxB
  have hc : 0 < C + S := by linarith
  have hord := power_order C S H Ts B W k A x hC hS hH hTs hk hB hix hxB
  refine ⟨power_change C S H Ts W k A x (ne_of_gt hc), hord.2, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have hd : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc initialTemperature B,
        HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
          (C / netPower W k A y -
           C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) y := by
      intro y hy
      have ho := power_order C S H Ts B W k A y hC hS hH hTs hk hB hy.1 hy.2
      exact boiling_time_derivative C S H Ts B W k A y (ne_of_gt hc)
        (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt ho.1) (ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le ho.1 ho.2))
    have hm : MonotoneOn (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
        (Set.Icc initialTemperature B) := by
      apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
      · intro y hy
        exact (hd y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
      · intro y hy
        exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
      · intro y hy
        have hmem := interior_subset hy
        have ho := power_order C S H Ts B W k A y hC hS hH hTs hk hB hmem.1 hmem.2
        have hz : 0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y) :=
          lt_of_lt_of_le ho.1 ho.2
        have he : C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y) ≤
            C / netPower W k A y := by
          apply (div_le_div_iff₀ hz ho.1).2
          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ho.2 (le_of_lt hC)
        linarith
    exact hm ⟨le_refl _, le_trans hix hxB⟩ ⟨hix, hxB⟩ hix
  · unfold heatingTime
    rw [sub_self, mul_zero]

import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring

/- Supplied starting temperature in degrees Celsius. -/
def initialTemperature : ℝ := 20

/- Constant heater input W, room temperature A, linear heat-loss
   coefficient k. This SAME law applies to water and brine (watts). -/
def netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)

/- Instantaneous conservation of energy on adding salt: C is water+pot
   capacity, S = final solution capacity minus original water capacity (signed),
   Ts salt temperature and enthalpy reference, H dissolution energy at Ts. Capacities J/K, H joules. -/
noncomputable def mixedTemperature (C S H Ts x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (C * x + S * Ts - H) / (C + S)

/- Integrated inverse energy balance dt/dT = capacity/netPower(T).
   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/
noncomputable def heatingTime (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  capacity / k * (Real.log (netPower W k A u) - Real.log (netPower W k A v))

/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when
   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The mixing temperature jump and the
   changed heat capacity are both included. -/
noncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +
  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B

/- H is the isothermal dissolution energy at Ts, not at every x.
   If cs is solid salt capacity, Kirchhoff gives dissolution energy
   H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts) at x. Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).
   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/
lemma reference_consistent_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +
      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔
      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by
  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  rw [eq_div_iff hc]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/
lemma mixing_balance :
    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by
  intro C S H Ts x hc
  unfold mixedTemperature
  field_simp

/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared
   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/
lemma power_change :
    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by
  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc
  unfold netPower mixedTemperature
  field_simp
  ring

lemma power_derivative :
    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by
  intro W k A x
  unfold netPower
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp

/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:
   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/
lemma heating_time_derivative :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)
      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv
  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub
    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)
  unfold heatingTime
  convert h using 1
  field_simp [hk, hv]

/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.
   For any elapsed-time curve f with df/dT = capacity/netPower and f(u)=0,
   the endpoint time MUST equal heatingTime; it is not a fitted formula.
   Endpoint derivatives may be read as those of a smooth local extension. -/
lemma stage_time_from_energy :
    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),
    u ≤ v → k ≠ 0 →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt f (capacity / netPower W k A y) y) →
    f u = 0 → f v = heatingTime capacity W k A u v := by
  intro capacity W k A u v f huv hk hp hf hu
  have mono : ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ),
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt g 0 y) → MonotoneOn g (Set.Icc u v) := by
    intro g hg
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hg y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact le_refl 0
  have hd : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v,
      HasDerivAt (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) 0 y := by
    intro y hy
    have hh := heating_time_derivative capacity W k A u y hk (ne_of_gt (hp y hy))
    convert (hf y hy).sub hh using 1 <;> simp
  have hm := mono (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) hd
  have hn := mono (fun w => -(f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w)) (by
    intro y hy
    convert (hd y hy).neg using 1 <;> simp)
  have hle := hm ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hge := hn ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv
  have hzero : heatingTime capacity W k A u u = 0 := by
    simp only [heatingTime, sub_self, mul_zero]
  linarith

/- Eliminate the two heating stages. The derivative compares the time
   spent heating unsalted water with the time saved in the salted stage. -/
lemma boiling_time_derivative :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C / netPower W k A x -
       C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hm : HasDerivAt (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) (C / (C + S)) x := by
    unfold mixedTemperature
    convert ((((hasDerivAt_id x).const_mul C).add_const (S * Ts)).sub_const H).div_const
      (C + S) using 1 <;> simp
  have hn := (power_derivative W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)).comp x hm
  have hpost := (((hn.log hz).sub_const
    (Real.log (netPower W k A B))).const_mul ((C + S) / k))
  have hpre := heating_time_derivative C W k A initialTemperature x hk hx
  convert hpre.add hpost using 1
  · rfl
  · dsimp only [Function.comp_apply]
    field_simp [hc, hk, hx, hz]
    ring

/- The derivative has precisely the sign of the net cooling energy
   D(x)=S*(x-Ts)+H when capacities and net powers are positive. -/
lemma timing_derivative_signed :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 → k ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A x ≠ 0 →
    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) ≠ 0 →
    HasDerivAt (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A)
      (C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x))) x := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz
  have hj := power_change C S H Ts W k A x hc
  have he : C / netPower W k A x - C / netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) =
      C * (k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
        (netPower W k A x * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x)) := by
    rw [← hj]
    field_simp
    <;> ring
  rw [← he]
  exact boiling_time_derivative C S H Ts B W k A x hc hk hx hz

/- Constant-capacity mixing is increasing in the addition temperature,
   even if S<0. Endpoint constraints keep the entire trajectory liquid.
   F is a common liquid lower bound; B0 is unsalted boiling temperature. -/
lemma feasible_trajectory :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    y ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (initialTemperature ≤ y ∧ y ≤ B0) ∧
    (F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ∧ mixedTemperature C S H Ts y ≤ B) ∧
    (0 < netPower W k A y ∧ 0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy
  have hzmono : Monotone (mixedTemperature C S H Ts) := by
    intro a b hab
    unfold mixedTemperature
    exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hc).2 (by nlinarith)
  have hzlo := le_trans hzl (hzmono hy.1)
  have hzhi := le_trans (hzmono hy.2) hzu
  refine ⟨⟨le_trans hi hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hU⟩, ⟨hzlo, hzhi⟩, ?_⟩
  unfold netPower at *
  constructor <;> nlinarith [hy.2]

/- Comparing stages on any feasible subinterval, using the derived sign. -/
lemma time_increasing_on_cooling :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      exact div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hC)
        (div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
        (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
  exact hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv

lemma time_decreasing_on_warming :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A u v : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k → u ≤ v →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) →
    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
    boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv hp hs
  have hd := fun y hy => timing_derivative_signed C S H Ts B W k A y
    (ne_of_gt hc) (ne_of_gt hk) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).1) (ne_of_gt (hp y hy).2)
  have hm : MonotoneOn (fun y => -boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A y) (Set.Icc u v) := by
    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y hy).neg.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      exact (hd y (interior_subset hy)).neg.hasDerivWithinAt
    · intro y hy
      have hm := interior_subset hy
      have hn : C * (k * (S * (y - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) /
          (netPower W k A y * netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y)) ≤ 0 :=
        div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
          (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hC)
            (div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg
              (mul_nonpos_of_nonneg_of_nonpos (le_of_lt hk) (hs y hm)) (le_of_lt hc)))
          (le_of_lt (mul_pos (hp y hm).1 (hp y hm).2))
      exact neg_nonneg.mpr hn
  have hh := hm ⟨le_refl _, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl _⟩ huv
  linarith

/- Conditional scientific answer over an explicitly feasible interval.
   S>=0: earliest, latest, or interior root as D changes sign.
   S<=0: compare endpoint boiling times. S=H=0: all schedules tie.
   H is allowed either sign; mixing need not cool or increase net power. -/
theorem addition_timing_answer :
    ∀ (C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x : ℝ),
    0 < C → 0 < C + S → 0 < k →
    F ≤ initialTemperature → initialTemperature ≤ L → L ≤ U → U ≤ B0 →
    F ≤ mixedTemperature C S H Ts L → mixedTemperature C S H Ts U ≤ B →
    0 < netPower W k A U → 0 < netPower W k A B →
    x ∈ Set.Icc L U →
    (netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =
      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S)) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → 0 ≤ S * (L - Ts) + H →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 ≤ S → S * (U - Ts) + H ≤ 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (0 < S → Ts - H / S ∈ Set.Icc L U →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A (Ts - H / S) ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S ≤ 0 →
      min (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L) (boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A U) ≤
        boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) ∧
    (S = 0 → H = 0 →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A L = boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A x) := by
  intro C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U x hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hx
  have hp : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc L U, 0 < netPower W k A y ∧
      0 < netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts y) := by
    intro y hy
    exact (feasible_trajectory C S H Ts B W k A F B0 L U y
      hC hc hk hF hi hLU hU hzl hzu hpU hpB hy).2.2
  have inc : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 ≤ S * (y - Ts) + H) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_increasing_on_cooling C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  have dec : ∀ u v, L ≤ u → v ≤ U → u ≤ v →
      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, S * (y - Ts) + H ≤ 0) →
      boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A v ≤ boilingTime C S H Ts B W k A u := by
    intro u v hlu hvu huv hs
    apply time_decreasing_on_warming C S H Ts B W k A u v hC hc hk huv
    · intro y hy
      exact hp y ⟨le_trans hlu hy.1, le_trans hy.2 hvu⟩
    · exact hs
  refine ⟨power_change C S H Ts W k A x (ne_of_gt hc), ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hS hD
    apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hD
    apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
    intro y hy
    nlinarith [hy.2]
  · intro hS hr
    have hroot : S * ((Ts - H / S) - Ts) + H = 0 := by
      field_simp
      <;> ring
    by_cases hxr : x ≤ Ts - H / S
    · apply dec x (Ts - H / S) hx.1 hr.2 hxr
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply inc (Ts - H / S) x hr.1 hx.2 (le_of_not_ge hxr)
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS
    by_cases hD : 0 ≤ S * (x - Ts) + H
    · apply le_trans (min_le_left _ _)
      apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      nlinarith [hy.2]
    · apply le_trans (min_le_right _ _)
      apply dec x U hx.1 (le_refl _) hx.2
      intro y hy
      have hh := le_of_not_ge hD
      nlinarith [hy.1]
  · intro hS hH
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply inc L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]
    · apply dec L x (le_refl _) hx.2 hx.1
      intro y hy
      simp [hS, hH]

  "content": "import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Deriv\nimport Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.MeanValue\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp\nimport Mathlib.Tactic.Ring\n\n/- Supplied starting temperature in degrees Celsius. -/\ndef initialTemperature : ℝ := 20\n\n/- Constant heater input W, room temperature A, linear heat-loss\n   coefficient k. This SAME law applies to water and brine (watts). -/\ndef netPower (W k A T : ℝ) : ℝ := W - k * (T - A)\n\n/- Instantaneous conservation of energy on adding salt: C is water+pot\n   capacity, S = final solution capacity minus original water capacity (signed),\n   Ts salt temperature and enthalpy reference, H dissolution energy at Ts. Capacities J/K, H joules. -/\nnoncomputable def mixedTemperature (C S H Ts x : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n  (C * x + S * Ts - H) / (C + S)\n\n/- Integrated inverse energy balance dt/dT = capacity/netPower(T).\n   Used only where net power is positive and k>0. -/\nnoncomputable def heatingTime (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n  capacity / k * (Real.log (netPower W k A u) - Real.log (netPower W k A v))\n\n/- Total seconds to a fixed final solution boiling temperature B when\n   salt is added at unsalted temperature x. The mixing temperature jump and the\n   changed heat capacity are both included. -/\nnoncomputable def boilingTime (C S H Ts B W k A x : ℝ) : ℝ :=\n  heatingTime C W k A initialTemperature x +\n  heatingTime (C + S) W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) B\n\n/- H is the isothermal dissolution energy at Ts, not at every x.\n   If cs is solid salt capacity, Kirchhoff gives dissolution energy\n   H+(S-cs)*(x-Ts) at x. Warming the solid to x costs cs*(x-Ts).\n   Thus their sum is H+S*(x-Ts), for either sign of S. -/\nlemma reference_consistent_balance :\n    ∀ (C S H Ts cs x z : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →\n    ((C + S) * (z - x) + cs * (x - Ts) +\n      (H + (S - cs) * (x - Ts)) = 0 ↔\n      z = mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) := by\n  intro C S H Ts cs x z hc\n  unfold mixedTemperature\n  rw [eq_div_iff hc]\n  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith\n\n/- Derived conservation of enthalpy; no presumed mixing-temperature sign. -/\nlemma mixing_balance :\n    ∀ (C S H Ts x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →\n    (C + S) * mixedTemperature C S H Ts x = C * x + S * Ts - H := by\n  intro C S H Ts x hc\n  unfold mixedTemperature\n  field_simp\n\n/- Derive the net-power jump from energy conservation AND the shared\n   heat-transfer law; before/after powers are not independent parameters. -/\nlemma power_change :\n    ∀ (C S H Ts W k A x : ℝ), C + S ≠ 0 →\n    netPower W k A (mixedTemperature C S H Ts x) - netPower W k A x =\n      k * (S * (x - Ts) + H) / (C + S) := by\n  intro C S H Ts W k A x hc\n  unfold netPower mixedTemperature\n  field_simp\n  ring\n\nlemma power_derivative :\n    ∀ (W k A x : ℝ), HasDerivAt (netPower W k A) (-k) x := by\n  intro W k A x\n  unfold netPower\n  convert (((hasDerivAt_id x).sub_const A).const_mul k).const_sub W using 1 <;> simp\n\n/- Checks the integrated heating law against the differential first law:\n   increasing endpoint temperature costs capacity/netPower seconds/K. -/\nlemma heating_time_derivative :\n    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ), k ≠ 0 → netPower W k A v ≠ 0 →\n    HasDerivAt (fun y => heatingTime capacity W k A u y)\n      (capacity / netPower W k A v) v := by\n  intro capacity W k A u v hk hv\n  have h := (((power_derivative W k A v).log hv).const_sub\n    (Real.log (netPower W k A u))).const_mul (capacity / k)\n  unfold heatingTime\n  convert h using 1\n  field_simp [hk, hv]\n\n/- Derivation of the stage-time formula from the inverse first law.\n   For any elapsed-time curve f with df/dT = capacity/netPower and f(u)=0,\n   the endpoint time MUST equal heatingTime; it is not a fitted formula.\n   Endpoint derivatives may be read as those of a smooth local extension. -/\nlemma stage_time_from_energy :\n    ∀ (capacity W k A u v : ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),\n    u ≤ v → k ≠ 0 →\n    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, 0 < netPower W k A y) →\n    (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt f (capacity / netPower W k A y) y) →\n    f u = 0 → f v = heatingTime capacity W k A u v := by\n  intro capacity W k A u v f huv hk hp hf hu\n  have mono : ∀ (g : ℝ → ℝ),\n      (∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v, HasDerivAt g 0 y) → MonotoneOn g (Set.Icc u v) := by\n    intro g hg\n    apply monotoneOn_of_hasDerivWithinAt_nonneg (convex_Icc _ _)\n    · intro y hy\n      exact (hg y hy).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt\n    · intro y hy\n      exact (hg y (interior_subset hy)).hasDerivWithinAt\n    · intro y hy\n      exact le_refl 0\n  have hd : ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc u v,\n      HasDerivAt (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) 0 y := by\n    intro y hy\n    have hh := heating_time_derivative capacity W k A u y hk (ne_of_gt (hp y hy))\n    convert (hf y hy).sub hh using 1 <;> simp\n  have hm := mono (fun w => f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w) hd\n  have hn := mono (fun w => -(f w - heatingTime capacity W k A u w)) (by\n    intro y hy\n    convert (hd y hy).neg using 1 <;> simp)\n  have hle := hm ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv\n  have hge := hn ⟨le_refl u, huv⟩ ⟨huv, le_refl v⟩ huv\n  have hzero : heatingTime capacity W k A u u = 0 := by\n    simp only [heatingTime, sub_self, mul_zero]\n  linarith\n\n/- Eliminate the two heating stages.
